R1.correction: one `named()` function applied at every public entry -- place, status_name, record_capture, capture_state, read, follow -- and at the two internals that join a suffix, before a descriptor is opened or a room is held
R1.the_pattern: THE THIRD APPEARANCE OF ONE MISTAKE. I confined the streams, then the metadata about them, and left the public reader operands unconfined. `place` held the allowlist and nothing else called it.
R1.what: a stream operand reached the filesystem without passing the allowlist, so read(delivery, '../other') returned a sibling's log from outside the attempt's room
R1.why_descriptor_relative_was_not_enough: O_NOFOLLOW governs the FINAL component only and dir_fd resolves '..' like any path, so a parent-relative or absolute operand walks straight out of a held room. The ALLOWLIST is the confinement.

R2.correction: creation ownership is tracked and only an entry this call made is ever unlinked; the staging identity is per CALL (pid plus a module counter)
R2.fixture_note: the per-call counter also makes the staging name unguessable from outside, so the collision cases patch the module's own `_STAGING` seam rather than guessing a name
R2.second_half: the staging name was os.getpid(), which every thread in a process shares, and the tee this delivery exists for is two threads draining two streams at once
R2.what: the failure handler unlinked the staging entry on ANY failure, including the FileExistsError from the exclusive create itself -- so a refusal to touch somebody else's entry deleted it

R3.correction: every byte is written before the replace; no progress is a failure rather than a reason to ask forever; nothing is published unless it was written whole, so a valid declaration already recorded survives a failed attempt to replace it
